english.title: Responsible person fail to arrange veterinary surgeon to implant transponder
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the

(A)_[owner having primary day-to-day responsibility for an equine, namely **(..SPECIFY EQUINE..), that was deemed to be identified in accordance with Articles 4(2) or 43(1) of the Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/262,]_
(B)_[keeper of an equine, namely **(..SPECIFY EQUINE..), that was deemed to be identified in accordance with Articles 4(2) or 43(1) of the Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/262 and for which the owner did not have primary day-to-day responsibility,]_

failed to arrange, for the purposes of Article 18(5) of that Regulation, for a veterinary surgeon to implant a transponder into that equine when

(C)_[a previously implanted and recorded transponder had ceased to function]_
(D)_[the equine arrived in Wales having been subject to an alternative method of identity verification authorised by a member State under Article 21]_
(E)_[had not already had a transponder implanted as required and was born on or before 30th June 2019]_
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 13(3), 22 and 34 of the Equine Identification (Wales) Regulations 2019.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
responsible person for equine
which has a previously implanted and recorded transponder that has ceased to function OR
which has been subject to an alternative method of identity verification authorised by a member State under Article 21 of the Commission Implementing Regulation (EU 2015 / 262) OR
which has not already had a transponder implanted in compliance with requirements and was born on or before 30 June 2009
failed to arrange for veterinary surgeon
to implant a transponder into the equine

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 monthsNote
